author: Hannah J Davies
description:
You definitely won’t be bored by the TV take on the first of the Dublin Trilogy novels. But you might well feel confused by this Bonnie and Clyde-style caper through gangland Ireland (featuring Aidan Gillen)

Tall Tales and Murder is likely to elicit varied responses from viewers, but boredom will surely be low on the list. This Irish caper – based on the first of the Dublin Trilogy novels by Caimh McDonnell, and written for TV by Stuart Carolan – moves at a mile a minute, taking in disgruntled gangsters; a dysfunctional care home; buried treasure; bedroom cuckoldry; a Paul Mescal lookalike contest and much more. Billed as a Bonnie and Clyde-style escapade, there are hints of Channel 4’s offbeat hit The End of the F***ing World, BBC Scotland’s thriller
title: Tall Tales and Murder review – this Irish version of The Wire makes for mile-a-minute TV

author: David Hytner at Old Trafford
description:
Michael Carrick enjoyed one of his finest nights as a Manchester United player in the Champions League against Roma, scoring twice in a 7-1 win in the quarter-final, second leg in 2007. The re-run here was all about his managerial survival at the club.

The situation looked impossibly grim for him at half-time. Amid an atmosphere of continued fan anger towards the United ownership, Carrick’s team had been implausibly bad. Roma took a 2-0 lead into the break and the truth was that the scoreline greatly flattered United.

Continue reading...
title: Manchester United produce comeback for the ages as Cunha double floors Roma

author: Leyland Cecco in Toronto
description:
The incident took place in the same province where a grizzly attacked a group of schoolchildren last November

A mother is dead and her daughter is missing in western Canada after a suspected grizzly bear attack in the same community where a bear attacked a group of schoolchildren earlier in the year.

On Tuesday, the British Columbia conservation officer service said in a social media post that it had launched a search for the two missing people on the weekend, and that during the search on Sunday an officer found the mother’s body. The search for her 19-year-old daughter is ongoing.

Continue reading...
title: One dead and another missing in suspected grizzly bear attack in Canada

author: Reuters
description:
Triumphal arch continues to face legal challenges as government says DC area project will take up to 39 months

The US justice department said on Tuesday that Donald Trump’s proposed 250ft (76 meter) triumphal arch in Washington would not be completed until after the end of his second term.

If it is given ⁠the go-ahead, the ⁠justice department said it ​expected an initial six to eight months of construction focused on excavation and foundation work that could begin as soon as Thursday, with above-ground construction ⁠beginning in May 2027 at the earliest. Total construction is anticipated to take 33 to 39 months, the government said.

Continue reading...
title: DoJ says Trump’s proposed 250ft arch would be completed after end of his term

author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
description:
Akande serving at international court of justice comes a decade after previous British judge failed to get re-elected

A British judge has been elected on to the UN’s international court of justice, in a big British diplomatic victory that comes almost 10 years after a previous British judge failed to get re-elected.

Dapo Akande will now serve as one of the ICJ’s 15 judges for a minimum nine-year term.

Continue reading...
title: British lawyer Dapo Akande elected to UN top court in big diplomatic win

author: Ed Aarons in Prague
description:
• Defender travelled with squad after long injury absence

  • ‘I have clips’: Arteta hits back after Liverpool complaints

Mikel Arteta is confident that William Saliba is ready to make his first appearance of the season for Arsenal after he played 45 minutes of a match behind closed doors last week.

The France defender started training on his own last month after the back injury he sustained at the World Cup but has since resumed full training and on Tuesday travelled with Arsenal’s squad to face Slavia Prague. It remains to be seen whether Saliba will feature in the Czech capital given such a lengthy absence, although Arteta insisted that he has no doubts the 25-year-old is primed to return.

Continue reading...
title: Arteta backs Saliba’s readiness to return for Arsenal at Slavia Prague

author: Kiran Stacey and Lisa O’Carroll
description:
Agriculture, youth visas and emissions agreements nearly tied up under PM’s plan for a much closer relationship with Brussels

  • The UK-EU food produce deal: what was agreed and will it affect shoppers?

Andy Burnham is preparing to announce billions of pounds of trade deals with the EU covering everything from youth visas to pet passports under his vision of a much closer relationship with the bloc.

With the prime minister scheduled to meet his European counterparts in Brussels on 20 November, officials have all but agreed three deals that would allow farmers to sell freely to the continent and travellers to take their animals abroad more easily.

Continue reading...
title: Andy Burnham to unveil EU trade deals worth billions of pounds

author: Edward Helmore
description:
Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory is expected to re-enter Earth’s atmosphere Wednesday, burning up in the process

Nasa’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, which has spent two decades studying the most powerful explosions in the cosmos, is expected to re-enter the Earth’s atmosphere on Wednesday, burning up in the process.

The satellite, which was designed to operate with its three telescopes for just two years, is no longer able to steer or observe, and its re-entry is uncontrolled.

Continue reading...
title: Nasa telescope launched in 2004 to plunge back to Earth after failed rescue mission

author: Associated Press
description:
Jacob Morley, serving a life sentence for killing a co-worker, slipped through a prison fence last week

A man convicted of murder who escaped from a Tennessee prison was recaptured on Tuesday in Missouri after more than a week on the run, authorities said.

Jacob Morley, who was serving a life sentence for killing a co-worker four years ago, was apprehended outside Kansas City, Missouri, before midday by the state highway patrol.

Continue reading...
title: Convicted murderer who escaped from Tennessee prison captured in Missouri

author: Dan Milmo Global technology editor
description:
Firm reveals details about how its cryptocurrency exchange was compromised, saying operation began in June

The hackers behind the $6.3bn (£4.7bn) Binance heist used bogus job interviews, malicious software and an internal AI tool, the company has revealed.

The world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange was compromised in an operation that began with an inadvertent download of malware in June, led to a recruitment scam in September and then a raid last week of “hot wallets” where billions of dollars worth of crypto-assets were taken.

Continue reading...
title: Hackers behind $6.3bn Binance heist ‘used malware and bogus job interviews’

author: Emma Loffhagen
description:
A Court of Splintered Harmony also records biggest single week of sales since Harper Lee’s Go Set a Watchman in 2015

Sarah J Maas’s long-awaited return to her bestselling romantasy series has smashed UK sales records, with A Court of Splintered Harmony becoming the fastest-selling adult fantasy novel since accurate records began in 1998.

The novel, the sixth in Maas’s A Court of Thorns and Roses (Acotar) series and her first return to it in more than five years, sold 188,914 copies in the UK between publication day on 27 October and 31 October, according to NielsenIQ BookData. That also makes it the fastest-selling hardback novel since Dan Brown’s Inferno, which sold 229,000 copies in its first week in 2013.

Continue reading...
title: Latest Sarah J Maas book becomes UK’s fastest-selling adult fantasy novel

author: Andy Hunter in Istanbul
description:
• Reds target fourth straight Champions League win

  • Turkish side led by ex-Liverpool forward Dirk Kuyt

Andoni Iraola has said Liverpool must improve their attacking play but dismissed concerns over the contrast between his team’s output in the Premier League and Champions League.

Liverpool boast a 100% record in Europe this season and can take a significant step towards qualification for the knockout phase with victory away at Fenerbahce on Wednesday. Former Liverpool favourite Dirk Kuyt will take charge of his first European game with the Turkish club, having replaced Ismail Kartal on an interim basis last week.

Continue reading...
title: Andoni Iraola calls on Liverpool to sharpen up in attack before Fenerbahce test

author: Editorial
description:
Andy Burnham’s commitment to a structured dialogue with Caribbean governments is a step forward, but they need more than words

There was a risk, in the run-up to the Commonwealth heads of government meeting (Chogm) this week, that important discussions could be derailed by the UK government’s refusal to apologise for slavery and the slave trade, combined with its continuing rejection of calls for financial reparations. For the Caribbean governments and campaigners pushing for these steps, the siting of the biennial gathering in Antigua and Barbuda offered a vital opportunity to press their case and raise awareness of the challenges that they face.

That deadlock was broken when Andy B
title: The Guardian view on apologising for slavery: a necessary process has at last begun | Editorial

author: Editorial
description:
The latest edition of Radical Thinking, the Guardian’s new podcast, should be required listening at a Treasury still stifled by outdated orthodoxies

As prime ministers have come and gone at bewildering speed in recent years, the search for elusive economic growth has become the overriding fixation of the British political class. In the lead-up to the 2024 general election, Sir Keir Starmer declared that “growth must become Labour’s obsession”, given the financial constraints that any new government would be under. The scale of Labour’s progressive offer, it was made clear, would be umbilically linked to its ability to generate a significant uptick in GDP.

“Growth in every postcode” is also the early mantra of Andy Burnham’s government. The prime minister swept to powe
title: The Guardian view on Labour’s growth obsession: a different economics is possible | Editorial

author: Rafael Behr
description:
It will take decades to rebuild trust in a country that removed a tyrant once – and then reinstated him four years later

When Joe Biden entered the White House in 2021 it was possible to believe that Donald Trump’s reign had been an aberration. “America is back. The transatlantic alliance is back,” the new president declared to relieved European leaders shortly after winning the 2020 race. It was true, but not for long.

Trump’s defeat proved that US democracy was mechanically operational, not culturally robust. His supporters tried violent subversion to prevent the inauguration of a successor. A second term should have been unthinkable. Republicans who failed to denounce the 6 January insurrection should have been unelectable. Instead, within four years, US voters reinstated the champion of a failed coup against their cherished constitution as commander-in-chief.
title: Even if US democracy can be salvaged from Trump, Europe is moving on | Rafael Behr

author: Gerard Meagher
description:
• Smith’s calf injury to be tested in training on Wednesday

  • Alex Mitchell ruled out of Nations Championship finals

Fin Smith faces a make-or-break training session on Wednesday to prove his fitness for the No 10 jersey in England’s autumn opener against Australia on Sunday, amid cautious optimism the Northampton playmaker will come through unscathed.

Smith sustained a calf injury in Northampton’s derby defeat by Leicester last month and the England head coach, Steve Borthwick, has been sweating on his fitness ever since. Smith’s Northampton half-back partner, Alex Mitchell, meanwhile, has been ruled out of England’s entire autumn campaign owing to his latest hamstring injury.

Continue reading...
title: England’s Fin Smith facing make-or-break fitness test before Australia clash

author: Michael Savage Media editor
description:
Person’s anonymity remains in place subject to any appeal against high court decision

A “well-known individual” has failed in his attempt to stop two media organisations from publishing allegations of inappropriate sexual activities towards young women, the high court has ruled.

The legal team for the anonymous individual, known in court only as PPT, had claimed he was “highly likely” to attempt suicide if the Guardian and ITN published the allegations, which he denies.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Well-known individual’ fails in bid for injunction against Guardian and ITN

author: Agencies
description:
• US set to host Summer and Winter Olympics

  • USOPC CEO says business model in early stages

The US Olympic and Paralympic Committee (USOPC) is in the advanced stages of setting up an entity to sell a stake ⁠in the commercial rights for Team USA in return for capital, according to multiple reports.

Any deal would mark a significant shift for the USOPC, a non-profit organization that, unlike many national Olympic committees, relies heavily on sponsorships, licensing ⁠and other commercial revenue streams rather than government funding.

Continue reading...
title: USOPC considering plan to sell stake in Team USA as LA Olympics approach

author: Natricia Duncan in St John's
description:
The king did not give explicit support for reparations but says he is committed to ‘addressing past wrongs’

King Charles has said that deepening his understanding of the horrors of slavery has made him more determined to address the wrongs of the past, as Caribbean leaders and campaigners intensified demands for an apology and reparations from Britain.

“We cannot change the actions of those who came before us,” Charles told leaders at the opening of the Commonwealth summit in Antigua and Barbuda on Tuesday. “We can, however, learn from the past.

title: King Charles addresses summit as campaigners intensify demands for apology for slavery

author: Gwyn Topham and Jamie Grierson
description:
Unclear if series of incidents affecting two UK departures and a number of Ryanair services among others are connected

  • Europe live – latest updates

At least seven planes around Europe were searched or diverted after a series of bomb threats to passenger flights on Tuesday.

Two UK departures and a number of Ryanair flights were threatened in what the UK government called “malicious hoaxes”, after all planes landed safely and no explosives were found.

Continue reading...
title: Seven planes across Europe searched or diverted after ‘malicious hoax’ bomb threats

author: Dan Milmo and Robert Booth
description:
Cybersecurity experts say national impact ‘minimal’ but incidents may represent the ‘foothills’ of a wider threat

Food suppliers in the UK have been hit by cyber-attacks after hackers raised the temperatures of supermarket freezers across Europe.

The UK’s National Cyber Security Centre (NSCS) said it was working with the affected companies but the national impact was minimal.

Continue reading...
title: Food suppliers in UK hit by cyber-attacks after freezers targeted in Europe

author: Andrew Roth
description:
US president makes surprise election day announcement, saying country does not ‘need’ $4bn annual payment

Donald Trump has said that the US will end military aid to Israel at the end of this year in a surprise election day announcement that appeared to be targeted at voters sceptical of US support for Israel and the war in Gaza.

In a phone interview with Fox News as voting began on Tuesday morning, the US president said the US would cut nearly $4bn (£2.96bn) in military aid to Israel because “they don’t need it”.

Continue reading...
title: Trump claims US will end military aid to Israel by end of this year

author: Ivana Rihter
description:
People everywhere are searching for the reason behind their sudden bursts of anguish or homesickness

  • Women: was your autoimmune condition misdiagnosed?

Some say it feels like a sudden burst of anguish; others liken it more to homesickness. The sudden onset of a sinking, upsetting feeling due to nipple stimulation is anecdotally known as Sad Nipple Syndrome (SNS), and for Sandra, it can be triggered by something as commonplace as putting on a shirt.

“I was probably a child when I first noticed: ‘Why does touching my nipple make me sad?’” says the 28-year-old. The sensation seemed to happen at random, and without the words to describe it, she kept it a secret.
title: ‘The nipple touch of doom’: what is sad nipple syndrome and what causes it?

author: Arwa Mahdawi
description:
These resource-guzzling centres drive up utility bills and are hated across the political spectrum. Cue a clunky, but potentially influential, new name for them

Jesus may have turned water into wine, but Donald Trump has done one better: he turned Lake Ontario into Lake America and the Gulf of Mexico into the Gulf of America. And then, for his next trick, he insisted we all stop talking about artificial intelligence (AI) and call it superintelligence (SI) instead.

Those, of course, are only a few of the name changes the president has ushered in. When he’s not golfing or commenting on senators’ buttocks, president Trump loves a rebranding project. Which makes sense: coming up with a new name is far easier than making meaningful improvements to people’s lives
title: Datacentres are deeply unpopular – so the geniuses at OpenAI are rebranding them | Arwa Mahdawi

description:
Are you getting your RDA (recommended dose of art)? Along with 10,000 steps and five fruit and veg a day, this small, enjoyable change could make you much healthier – and happier

Name: Art.

Age: Art has been around for thousands of years. The drawings in Blombos Cave in South Africa, for example, are estimated to be about 73,000 years old. But this is less about how old and more about how often, and for how long.

author: Peter Walker
description:
George Madgwick, party leader on Hampshire county council, faces charges related to four teenagers between 2008 and 2021

Reform UK’s leader on Hampshire county council has been charged with 12 counts of rape and one of distributing indecent images of a child.

George Madgwick, 37, who is a councillor in Portsmouth and leads the Reform group on the council, was a prominent voice linked to recent protests in the town connected to the arrival of asylum seekers on small boats.

author: Emine Sinmaz
description:
Judge tells jurors he will be able to accept only a unanimous decision on seven charges against the comedian

The jury in Russell Brand’s rape and sexual assault trial has retired to consider its verdicts.

Brand, 51, has been described as a ruthless, calculated and manipulative sexual predator during the three-week trial at Southwark crown court. The comedian is accused of seven offences, including rape and sexual assault, against six women in allegations spanning 10 years from 1999. He denies all the charges.

Continue reading...
title: Jury in Russell Brand rape and sexual assault trial retires to consider verdicts

description:
Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now!

While Football Daily hasn’t actually seen much of West Ham this season, we’ve noted enough of their results to presume they were doing OK in their attempt to bounce back to the Premier League after relegation. author: Matthew Pearce
description:
British Veterinary Association president tells MPs surge in cases putting farmers under severe pressure and stress

The worst bluetongue season on record has been a major animal welfare crisis in Great Britain, MPs have been told, putting farmers under “severe emotional stress”.

Bluetongue, a viral disease that affects sheep, cattle and goats, can cause fever, lesions, stillbirths and death. The tongue may go blue and protrude from the mouth.

author: Alan Connor
description:
Puzzle solvers’ unique way of thinking was utilised as a recruiting tool for Bletchley Park. The true enigmas, though, are the people who come up with them in the first place

• Don’t get Cluesletter delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

The world of crossword setters is not enormous. A solver who had completed a puzzle which turned out to have been a recruiting tool for Bletchley Park recalled:

I was told, though not so primitively, that chaps with twisted brains like mine might be suitable for a particular type of work as a contribution to the war effort.

Take UMBRELLA at 77-Down. Today, crossword editors love to focus on a lively angle, such as the 2013 clue [Sidewalk cafe sight] or the trickier [Kind of insurance poli

author: Micha Frazer-Carroll in the Bahamas
description:
The British monarch has been stalked by protesters during his visit to the Bahamas, Antigua and Guyana – and they will only become more insistent as time goes on

• Don’t get Cotton Capital delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

The sun is starting to set in the Bahamas and the loud wash of the tide, which is always audible on Nassau’s Western Esplanade, is beginning to be drowned out by the sound of excited screams. King Charles is visiting the Caribbean archipelago, for which he is still the head of state, for the first time in more than 50 years and a youth rally attended by schoolchildren makes for a particularly welcoming crowd.

Some have described the king’s nine-day tour of the Bahamas, Antigua and Guyana amid growing calls for reparations as a

author: Niha Masih
description:
A previously unseen family archive offers a glimpse into the Indian Nobel prize winner’s artistic process and personal relationships in his final years

  • Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

It’s easy to run out of words to describe Rabindranath Tagore. The first non-European to win the Nobel prize in literature, Tagore was a Bengali poet, musician, novelist, philosopher, songwriter, painter, humanist and educator.

Born in 1861, Tagore left an indelible mark on the subcontinent’s literature, music, education and art. Among his enduring legacies are the national anthems of India and Bangladesh.

Continue reading...
title: The private creative world of Rabindranath Tagore, the man Yeats called ‘greater than any of us’

author: Hilary Osborne
description:
Ministers propose new guided retirement scheme to help give savers protection for life

  • Business live – latest updates

Millions of private sector workers will be offered a guaranteed pension income for life under new rules designed to help them get the most out of their retirement savings.

Over the past 30 years, the majority of final salary pension schemes offering a set payout for life have closed. Workers have instead saved into a scheme and arrived at retirement with a pot of money they have to decide what to do with.

Continue reading...
title: Guaranteed pension income ‘resurrected’ for 17m private sector workers

author: Melanie Wilkinson
description:
Long, short, tailored or sporty, there’s a great jacket for everyone – here are our favourites

• Jess Cartner-Morley’s November style essentials

It’s November, which means your thick tights and cosiest jumpers have emerged from that box under the bed. And while winter weather brings with it a whole host of wardrobe-related challenges, few can’t be solved with the addition of an outstanding coat.

A coat is the easiest way to add a stamp of your signature style to an outfit. They bring sophistication, drama, and (for some, most importantly) warmth. Elevate a simple jeans-and-tee outfit with a statement jacket, or pair a classic tailored option with a skirt and your favourite boots for an evening-out cheat code.
title: Faux fur, funnel necks and timeless wool: the 47 best women’s coats for autumn and winter

author: Emma Loffhagen
description:
The Guyana-born, British-based writer takes home the Royal Society of Literature prize honouring women writers over 60 who have broken barriers

The poet Grace Nichols has been named the winner of the 2026 Royal Society of Literature Pioneer prize, a £10,000 award that recognises women writers over 60 who broke through at a time when the literary world was less open to them.

Nichols, 76, who was born in Guyana and moved to the UK in 1977, made her name with I Is a Long-Memoried Woman, which took the Commonwealth poetry prize in 1983, and The Fat Black Woman’s Poems, a collection published the following year. Her poems have been GCSE set texts for decades, and she has written extensively for children as well as adults.

Continue reading...
title: ‘A trailblazer in the truest sense’: poet Grace Nichols wins £10,000 Pioneer prize

author: Blake Montgomery
description:
World’s largest crypto exchange faces fallout from angry customers, and Lula wins with WhatsApp

  • This was originally published in TechScape, a newsletter about how technology shapes our lives. Sign up to receive it here

This week in tech, we’re discussing the fallout from the multibillion-dollar hack of Binance and the significance of Lula’s political mobilization on WhatsApp.

And if you’ll be at Web Summit in Lisbon next week, drop me a line! I’ll be there moderating panels on open-source AI and human agency in the age of AI agents.
